# Pixelfork Car Physics
> Any car model (GLB) becomes a car that drives, or no model for a built-in low-poly car. The wheels are found automatically from the model's shape and turn and roll; a raycast vehicle gives it suspension, tyre grip, engine, gearbox, brakes and handbrake. Kerbs, ramps and jumps work. Works in any three.js page, and in game engines that already have a crashcat world.

- Use it (start here, ~140 lines, exact API with units and defaults): AI-GUIDE.md
- Machine-readable: dist/registry.json (version, needs, import names, presets, tuning ranges, controls)
- Types: dist/types.d.ts (modules "car", "car/engine-fx", "car/engine-sound")
- Load: an ES module, dist/car.module.js, through an import map that also maps "three" (0.186) and "crashcat" (0.0.5); it bundles neither
- Smallest complete example: demo/minimal.html — CAR.createPhysics({ floor: 400 }); CAR.create({ scene, physics }); car.drive({ throttle, brake, steer }); physics.step(1/60); physics.sync(alpha)
- Your own model: CAR.create({ scene, physics, model: gltf.scene }); check one with CAR.inspect(model); wrong front → forward: "-z"
- In a game with its own crashcat world object ({ world, layers, step, sync }): pass it as physics (AI-GUIDE §2)
- Camera: CAR.createCamera(camera, car) → cam.update(dt), cam.orbit(dx, dy), cam.zoom(f)
- Optional sound: "car/engine-fx" (pops, bangs, turbo; no files), "car/engine-sound" (recorded engine packs; loads files)
- Change the library: AGENTS.md
- Sibling libraries: Pixelfork Ragdoll, Pixelfork VFX Library, Pixelfork SFX Library, Pixelfork PBR Library
